_comment: Tier-2 for skfem hyperelasticity#6, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: use ib.interpolate(u) to get the displacement/gradient at quadrature points inside the form; touching u directly raises NameError, or with an outer closure computes against the LAST u instead of the current Newton iterate. Ran: MeshTri().refined(3), ElementVector(ElementTriP1), 162 DOFs, a bare undefined name in a kernel body, a form body that writes `u`, an assemble() with the state kwarg omitted, and six Newton steps toward a 10% stretch with the state passed through assemble(ib, disp=...) versus a factory-frozen closure. Printed: a bare undefined name raises NameError naming the identifier; a MISSING assemble kwarg raises KeyError naming 'disp'; but `u` itself IS bound inside a @BilinearForm (to the trial function), so writing u and meaning the displacement assembles a 162x162 matrix with no error at all -- a silent type confusion, not a NameError. The stale closure is the silent case: the kwarg Newton falls 2.14e-03 -> 4.29e-06 -> 4.09e-12 -> 5.03e-16 while the frozen closure returns EXACTLY 2.14e-03 at every one of six iterations, emits no warning, stays finite, and lands 6.4e-03 relative away from the correct solution.
